summary: Learn how real-time payments, CBDCs, APIs, and ISO 20022 affect bank risk. Build practical tools and policy outputs. Enquire today.
lede: Instant-payment risk management examines how faster settlement and payment-system changes can shift intraday liquidity, funding needs, and financial risk. For treasury and credit professionals and supervisors, this course offers a practical approach to assessing those effects through payment-flow mapping, liquidity-gap calculations, and disruption scenarios. It also covers ISO 20022 data lineage, CBDC and open banking risk assessment, and turning findings into policy and management reporting, using Basel III liquidity concepts as a reference point.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who evaluate how payment-system modernisation changes financial risk, supervision, and institutional planning. It suits intermediate practitioners who already work with credit portfolios, treasury processes, prudential analysis, or payment policy and need an integrated view.
prerequisites: You should have working exposure to credit risk, treasury, liquidity management, payment operations, financial supervision, or financial stability analysis. Familiarity with Basel III liquidity concepts, IFRS 9, or bank balance-sheet planning is helpful, but advanced quantitative modelling is not required. No programming is required for completion. Exercises use spreadsheet calculations, structured templates, and dashboard interpretation rather than software development. Advanced topics such as AI-assisted anomaly detection, CBDC architecture, and API integration receive conceptual and operational treatment, while policy mapping, scenario analysis, and reporting outputs receive hands-on practice.
topics: Digital financial services, payments & fintech risk
